The case checks pair with the converters below — isCamelCase, isSnakeCase, isKebabCase, isPascalCase and isConstantCase.
Arrays works on both lists and maps, and always hands back an array of the type you asked for.
findIndex, findValue and findValues compare Enums by their string value, so an enum case and its backing string match interchangeably.
The to… family casts a loose array into a typed one — the way request data becomes something a model can use: Plus the small maths helpers: sum, average, max, length, random and ge
Numbers parses, rounds and formats — including money, which it keeps in cents to avoid float drift: Money is stored as an integer number of cents, converted only at the edges:
Dictionary wraps an array of loose values — decoded JSON, a config block, a database row — and reads it as types, so nothing downstream deals with strings-that-might-be-numbers: Ne
Utils validates and parses the everyday user data — emails, phones, names and national IDs: The Argentine document helpers live here too — isValidDNI / dniToNumber and isValidCUIT
Safe encode and decode, reading and writing JSON files and urls, and decoding straight into a Dictionary:
